expectations.text: Report contains a SUMMARY section with numerical counts by category
expectations.evidence: Lines 16-26 contain an 'Extraction Summary' table with counts: Findings (5), Methods (4), Tensions (3), Implementation Ideas (1), Open Questions (1), Total extracted (14), Duplicates/overlaps (5), Net new items (9). Clear numerical breakdown by category.

expectations.text: Total extractions (claims + implementation ideas + tensions + enrichments + validations) >= 8
expectations.evidence: 14 total items extracted: 5 findings + 4 methods + 3 tensions + 1 implementation idea + 1 open question = 14, which is >= 8.

expectations.text: Skip rate is below 15% (skipped items / total candidates)
expectations.evidence: Only item #9 was marked 'SKIP — already well-covered.' 1 skipped out of 14 candidates = 7.1%, which is below 15%.

expectations.text: Every extracted item includes a rationale explaining why it was extracted
expectations.evidence: All 14 items include a 'Rationale' field with substantive explanations. For example, item #1 explains VocalMat's relevance to reproducibility and our ADR-003 threshold, item #6 explains why the parameter-free tension matters for honest cross-tool comparison, item #14 explains the local median filter's potential as a pre-CNN noise rejection step.

expectations.text: Extracted titles are phrased as claims/propositions, not topic labels
expectations.evidence: Checked representative titles: #1 'VocalMat adaptive thresholding eliminates user-defined parameters as the main source of USV detection variability' (proposition), #6 'VocalMat's parameter-free claim masks implicit parameters in morphological operations' (proposition), #13 'Comparison between VocalMat and DeepSqueak is not apples-to-apples because DeepSqueak can be retrained while VocalMat's pipeline is fixed' (proposition). All are claims/propositions, not topic labels.

expectations.text: At least 3 distinct categories are represented (e.g. core claims, implementation ideas, tensions)
expectations.evidence: 5 distinct categories present: Findings (5 items), Methods (4 items), Tensions (3 items), Implementation Ideas (1 item), Open Questions (1 item).

expectations.text: Report mentions checking existing notes for duplicates or overlap
expectations.evidence: Every item includes an 'Overlap check' field (e.g., item #1: 'No existing note covers adaptive thresholding or parameter-free detection... NEW'). Additionally, a 'Duplicate / Overlap Summary' table (lines 143-151) systematically maps extracted items to existing notes with overlap type classification.

expectations.text: The tension between discrete USV categories and continuous acoustic space is captured
expectations.evidence: Item #9: 'Discrete USV categories may lose information compared to continuous embeddings or latent representations' — explicitly captures this tension, noting 'The paper itself acknowledges that 11 discrete categories may not capture the full continuous variation.' Also supported by item #5 (UMAP/t-SNE overlap zones revealing continuous variation).
